  "endpoint_class": "not-stated",
  "concordance_definition": "The study defines success rates based on the probability of a drug advancing through clinical phases and ultimately gaining FDA approval. It differentiates between 'Phase Success' (transition to the next phase) and 'Likelihood of Approval' (LOA) from a given phase to FDA approval. The study emphasizes evaluating all indications ('development paths') rather than just the lead indication to more accurately reflect R&D productivity.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "Direct comparison of data and methodology on a year-by-year or decade-by-decade basis is difficult due to the timing of annotating suspended indications.",
    "Real-time data collection started in 2003, preventing direct comparison with prior decades using these data.",
    "The lead indication success rate is higher due to selection bias.",
    "Small sample sizes limit further analysis of failures by lead or nonlead indication, disease, modality, and company type.",
    "Public information is not always available to assess the degree of communication with regulators, adherence to recommendations, changes to prior standards, and input from phase 2 data for phase 3 study design.",
    "It was difficult to objectively determine if a phase 3 study did not reach an endpoint due to poor study design or the drug’s biological activity.",
    "The degree to which regulatory uncertainty factored into commercial decisions to not file for approval is unknown.",
    "The timing of annotating suspended indications and drugs is not precise enough to analyze yearly changes in success rates."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "The authors declare competing financial interests: details are available in the online version of the paper.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "10.4% of all indication development paths in phase 1 were approved by FDA.",
    "Phase I success (transition to phase 2) was 64.5%.",
    "Phase 2 success (transition to phase 3) was 32.4%.",
    "Phase 3 success (transition to NDA/BLA) was 60.1%.",
    "Probability of FDA approval after NDA/BLA submission was 83.2%.",
    "Lead indications had a LOA from phase 1 of 15.3%.",
    "Oncology drugs had the lowest LOA from phase 1 at 6.7%.",
    "Non-NMEs had the highest LOA from phase 1 of 20.0%.",
    "Biologics had nearly twice the LOA from phase 1 (14.6%) as NMEs (7.5%) for all indications.",
    "56.9% of all applications were approved on the first NDA/BLA submission.",
    "86.2% of applications were approved by the third submission.",
    "LOA from phase 1 for nonlead indications was 4.9%.",
    "835 companies and 7,372 independent drug development paths were analyzed from 2003 to 2011.",
    "The study analyzed 5,820 phase transitions."
  ]
}
